guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case is less about Kansas’ opening result and more about whether the market is discounting its offensive upside too heavily. Kansas generated 613 yards against Long Island, while new starting quarterback Isaiah Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns. We are not treating one game as proof, but that debut provides useful context for an offense our numbers expect to create scoring opportunities with reasonable consistency.

The supporting structure also matters. Nik McMillan opened his Kansas career with six catches for 130 yards and a touchdown, giving Marshall an immediate downfield option. Kansas has also allowed the second-fewest sacks in the Big 12 since the start of 2023. That combination of protection and explosive-play potential helps explain why our expectation is more favorable to Kansas than the market’s.

Our meaningful concern is Kansas’ pass defense, which remains one of the weaker units in our pass-EPA numbers. Arizona State has a plausible path to attacking that weakness, but our numbers are less impressed by its ability to turn possessions into sustained scoring opportunities. That tension matters, but we do not think it justifies the full degree of separation currently being priced.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Arizona State’s passing offense against the Kansas secondary. Kansas returns cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander after they combined for 22 starts last season, but experience alone does not erase the efficiency concerns in our numbers.

Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss and three sacks in its opener. The question for us is whether that disruption carries into a much more demanding matchup and keeps Arizona State from repeatedly testing the secondary. If Kansas can prevent clean, sustained passing possessions, our position becomes much easier to support.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 home win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, the eighth-highest single-game yardage total in program history.
Kansas rushed for 277 yards and five touchdowns against Long Island.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards, 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts and no touchdowns.
Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss and three sacks against Long Island.

opponent_notes.fact: Arizona State opened the 2026 season with a 70-7 win over Morgan State.
Arizona State is scheduled to play at Texas A&M on Sept. 12 before facing Kansas on Sept. 19.
Arizona State wide receiver Omarion Miller entered the week with consecutive 100-yard receiving games.

quarterback.fact: Kansas named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall its starting quarterback before the 2026 season, replacing a role primarily held by Jalon Daniels over the previous six seasons.
Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Redshirt junior Cole Ballard is the No. 2 quarterback on the Game 2 depth chart and entered the season with one career start.

Quarterback Chase Jenkins transferred from Rice after starting all 12 regular-season games there in 2025 and producing 1,025 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns, 531 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kansas returns two 2025 offensive-line starters: left tackle Calvin Clements and left guard Amir Herring, who each started all 12 games last season.

Kansas' Game 2 starting offensive line was listed as Calvin Clements at left tackle, Amir Herring at left guard, Kasen Carpenter at center, Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard and Nick Morrow at right tackle.
New center Kasen Carpenter transferred to Kansas after starting two games for Oklahoma State in 2025 and 11 games for Tulsa in 2024.
New right tackle Nick Morrow transferred from California after starting five games there in 2025.
Syracuse transfer Yasin Willis rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns in his Kansas debut against Long Island.
Kansas State transfer Dylan Edwards rushed six times for 32 yards in his Kansas debut.
Colorado State transfer Jalen Dupree rushed nine times for 35 yards and scored his first Kansas touchdown against Long Island.
Buffalo transfer Nik McMillan caught six passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in his Kansas debut, extending his streak to seven consecutive 100-yard receiving games.
Nahzae Cox recorded his first Kansas reception on a 47-yard pass from Isaiah Marshall against Long Island.

defensive_personnel.fact: Defensive end Leroy Harris III recorded a career-high four tackles for loss against Long Island after leading Kansas with 4.5 sacks in 2025.
Michigan State transfer David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in his Kansas debut.
Linebacker Trey Lathan returns after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025; he entered 2026 with 198 career tackles and 17 tackles for loss.
Kansas returns 2025 starting cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander, who combined for 22 starts last season.
Safety Taylor Davis returns after starting 10 games and recording 41 tackles, one interception and one pass breakup in 2025.
Kansas added experienced safeties Corey Gordon and Jaden Harris; Gordon started all 12 games for Louisville in 2025, while Harris previously started 13 games for Miami in 2024.
Redshirt freshman defensive end Garrett Martin recorded the first two tackles for loss of his career against Long Island.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach after spending the previous two seasons at Penn State.
Kotelnicki previously served as Kansas' offensive coordinator in 2021-22 and associate head coach/offensive coordinator in 2023.
D.K. McDonald is in his third season as Kansas' defensive coordinator.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett, who tied for the Kansas team lead with 45 receptions in 2025, did not play in the 2026 season opener.

Boston College transfer linebacker Bam Crouch started four games in 2025 before missing the remainder of that season due to injury; Kansas listed him atop an OR grouping at linebacker on its Game 2 depth chart.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas had six plays of at least 20 yards, including three plays of at least 40 yards, against Long Island.
Kansas' offensive line did not allow a sack and surrendered only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
Kansas has allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the second-fewest in the Big 12 over that span.
Kansas has averaged 19.7 yards per completion over the last two seasons.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas held Long Island to 1.1 yards per rushing attempt, allowing 35 yards on 33 carries.
Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 total yards per game in 2025.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025, fourth-most in the Big 12.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added kicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, punter Matt Gill from Australia and long snapper Rino Monteforte from California for 2026.
Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
Kansas listed Tate Nagy as its primary punt returner and Dylan Edwards as its primary kickoff returner on the Game 2 depth chart.

series_context.fact: Arizona State leads the series with Kansas 1-0 after defeating the Jayhawks 35-31 in Tempe in 2024.
The 2026 matchup will be the first Kansas-Arizona State meeting outside Tempe.

other_relevant.fact: Kansas and Arizona State are scheduled to play Sept. 19, 2026 at Wembley Stadium in London with an 11 a.m. Central kickoff.
The Kansas-Arizona State game will serve as the Big 12 opener for both teams.
The matchup will be the first international football game for both Kansas and Arizona State and the first college football game played at Wembley Stadium.
